vectors.name: indefinite-length-batch
vectors.note: An indefinite-length array of one empty map. Well-formed CBOR, and the same batch a definite-length encoder writes as 81a0 — which is why accepting it would mean two encodings of one batch.

vectors.name: indefinite-length-text-key
vectors.note: Chunked text, here one chunk spelling "a". Rule 1 covers strings as well as containers; a decoder that only checked array and map heads accepts this.

vectors.name: non-shortest-integer-head
vectors.note: Zero written with a one-byte head instead of the immediate 0x00.

vectors.name: non-shortest-length-head
vectors.note: Rule 2 covers lengths of major types 2-5, not only integer values: a one-signal batch whose array length is written 0x9801 rather than 0x81.

vectors.name: integer-above-i64-max
vectors.note: 2^63, the first unsigned CBOR integer outside i64. Shortest-head and definite-length: only rule 3 refuses it.

vectors.name: integer-below-i64-min
vectors.note: Major type 1 encodes -1-n, so this is -2^63-1: one below i64::MIN, whose own encoding is 0x3b7fffffffffffffff.

vectors.name: binary16-float
vectors.note: 1.5 as binary16. Exactly what RFC 8949 §4.2.1's shortest-float rule requires, and what §6.3.1 deviates from — see deviations.json.

vectors.name: binary32-float
vectors.note: 1.5 as binary32, the same value again. A decoder that widened either of these to binary64 would accept three encodings of one float.

vectors.name: nan
vectors.note: A quiet NaN. Rejected on arrival so that EXPR §9's "no NaN escapes" is a property of the type rather than an obligation on every builtin.

vectors.name: negative-infinity
vectors.note: Both infinities, because a sign-blind check on the exponent catches one and not the other.

vectors.name: signalling-nan
vectors.note: A signalling NaN has a different payload from a quiet one, and a check comparing against one NaN bit pattern rather than testing finiteness lets it through.

vectors.name: map-key-not-text
vectors.note: An integer key. CBOR permits any type; a signal is a map of text to value (§6.3).

vectors.name: map-keys-unsorted
vectors.note: "b" before "a". Descending is the easy case; the ordering deviation is in deviations.json.

vectors.name: map-keys-duplicated
vectors.note: Rejected rather than collapsed to the first or last: either choice re-encodes to bytes that did not arrive, which rule 7 says in as many words.

vectors.name: tagged-value
vectors.note: Tag 0 over a complete, canonical text string, so the tag is the only thing wrong with it. A decoder that skipped tags would accept two encodings of one string.

vectors.name: undefined
vectors.note: `undefined` is a simple value next to `null`, and the data model has one absent-ish value, not two.

vectors.name: unassigned-simple-value
vectors.note: Simple value 16, which is neither false, true nor null.

vectors.name: nesting-beyond-any-conforming-bound
vectors.note: Two hundred levels of nested array, asked of a decoder bounded at EXPR §9's floor. A host configured higher would accept it, so the vector states the bound it asserts at rather than assuming one; `depth` is clamped up to the floor, never down, so the floor is what this exercises.

vectors.name: trailing-bytes
vectors.note: The empty batch, complete and valid, followed by one byte. Corruption rather than a batch carrying extra data.

vectors.name: truncated-batch
vectors.note: A map promising one entry, a key, and no value. The other half of rule 10: a payload that ends early is corruption too.

vectors.name: array-length-claims-what-is-not-there
vectors.note: A nine-byte head claiming u64::MAX elements in a thirteen-byte payload. The assertion a runner cannot make from bytes alone is that this fails *without* allocating; what the vector pins is that it fails rather than hanging or dying.

vectors.name: byte-string-length-claims-what-is-not-there
vectors.note: The same hostile head on a byte string, where a decoder is most tempted to reserve the declared size up front.

vectors.name: batch-is-not-an-array
vectors.note: A bare map. A batch is an array of signals even when it holds one.

vectors.name: signal-is-not-a-map
vectors.note: An array of one integer. Signals are dict-shaped by definition (§6.3), so this is not a batch of one signal.

vectors.name: empty-input
vectors.note: No bytes at all is not the empty batch; the empty batch is 0x80.
